Skeleton

Plain shapes that stand where content is about to appear, so the page keeps its layout while it loads.

Status: draft

Examples

When to use it

  • While a list, a description or a block of content is fetched, when its shape is known and it usually arrives within a few seconds.
  • On the first load of a view. The shapes match what will replace them: as many rows as usually show, lines the length of the text.

When not to use it

  • When the shape of what is coming is not known, or the wait is an action the reader started. Use a spinner, with text that says what is happening.
  • When the wait has a measurable length, such as 7 of 12 checks. Use progress.
  • Together with a spinner for the same wait. Use one of the two.
  • After the fetch has failed, or after about ten seconds. Replace it with an error state that says what to do: a skeleton that never resolves is a broken promise.
  • While content already on screen is refreshed. Keep the content and set aria-busy on its container.
  • For text that is streaming in. Use streaming.

Variants

line ds-skeleton__line
A bar 12px tall in the space of one line of text, as wide as its container. For a paragraph or a set of facts, one above the other.
medium line ds-skeleton__line--medium
With ds-skeleton__line: 60% of the width, for a title or the last line of a paragraph.
short line ds-skeleton__line--short
With ds-skeleton__line: 35% of the width, for a label, a branch name or a time.
row ds-skeleton__row
A list row at least 44px tall, holding one or two lines. Its container also takes ds-skeleton--rows, so the rows touch and are divided by a rule, as list rows are.
block ds-skeleton__block
A rectangle 132px tall and as wide as its container, for a code block or a diff.

Accessibility

  • The container is a div with the ds-skeleton class and aria-busy="true". Its first child is a span with the ds-visually-hidden class that says what is loading, such as Loading tasks. The shapes are empty span elements and are not read out.
  • When the content arrives, the app replaces the whole container with it. Nothing of the skeleton stays, so aria-busy goes with it. When the skeleton stands inside a region that stays, such as a section with a heading, put aria-busy on that region and remove it when the content arrives.
  • When the fetch fails, or has taken about ten seconds, the app replaces the container with an error state that says what happened and offers Retry.
  • The shapes fade slowly between full and partial strength. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce the animation is off and the shapes hold still.
  • A skeleton has no controls and takes no focus. If the content it replaces had focus, move focus to the view's heading until the content is back.
  • The component needs no script beyond the app swapping it for the content.
